{{Short description|Class of complex vector function}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Jacobi form''' is an [[automorphic form]] on the [[Jacobi group]], which is the [[semidirect product]] of the [[symplectic group]] Sp(n;R) and the [[Heisenberg group]] <math>H^{(n,h)}_R</math>. The theory  was first systematically studied by {{harvtxt|Eichler|Zagier|1985}}.

==Definition==
A Jacobi form of level 1, weight ''k'' and index ''m'' is a function <math>\phi(\tau,z)</math> of two complex variables (with &tau; in the upper half plane) such that
*<math>\phi\left(\frac{a\tau+b}{c\tau+d},\frac{z}{c\tau+d}\right) = (c\tau+d)^ke^{\frac{2\pi i mcz^2}{c\tau+d}}\phi(\tau,z)\text{ for }{a\ b\choose c\ d}\in \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})</math>
*<math>\phi(\tau,z+\lambda\tau+\mu) = e^{-2\pi i m(\lambda^2\tau+2\lambda z)}\phi(\tau,z)</math> for all integers &lambda;, &mu;.
*<math>\phi</math> has a Fourier expansion 
:: <math>\phi(\tau,z) = \sum_{n\ge 0} \sum_{r^2\le 4mn} C(n,r)e^{2\pi i (n\tau+rz)}.</math>

==Examples==
Examples in two variables include [[Jacobi theta functions]], the [[Weierstrass P function|Weierstrass ℘ function]], and Fourier–Jacobi coefficients of [[Siegel modular form]]s of genus&nbsp;2. Examples with more than two variables include characters of some irreducible highest-weight representations of affine [[Kac–Moody algebra]]s. Meromorphic Jacobi forms appear in the theory of [[Mock modular form]]s.
